claims.claim: **Prophylaxis treats at-risk contacts to eliminate nasopharyngeal carriage**, cutting transmission and secondary cases. **Give it as soon as possible.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Prophylaxis goes early — to contacts and to the index case**, especially for *N. meningitidis*, because secondary cases can develop rapidly.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Local susceptibility patterns may change the choice** — check local guidelines.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **_N. meningitidis_ contacts needing prophylaxis:** close, prolonged contact from 7 days before symptom onset until 24 hours after the case's antibiotics began — household (highest risk); same childcare group (two full 6–8 hour days, or 20 hours cumulative); intimate (kissing); healthcare workers who had close, unprotected airway exposure without adequate PPE; passengers seated immediately next to the case for more than 8 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk of meningococcal disease is highest 7–10 days after exposure**; effective clearance antibiotics eliminate meningococci from the nasopharynx within 24 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ciprofloxacin, oral, single dose:** 30 mg/kg (max 125 mg) if under 5 years; 250 mg at 5–12 years; 500 mg from 12 years.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rifampicin, oral, twice daily for 2 days:** under 1 month 5 mg/kg; 1 month and over 10 mg/kg (max 600 mg).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rifampicin is preferred in neonates; ceftriaxone is preferred in pregnancy.** ⚠️ **Do not use rifampicin in pregnancy or severe liver disease.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pregnancy or rifampicin contraindicated: ceftriaxone IM, single dose** — 125 mg for 1 month to 12 years; 250 mg from 12 years.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer vaccination to non-immunised contacts** of serogroup A, C, W or Y cases.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The Hib index patient needs prophylaxis unless treated with ceftriaxone/cefotaxime.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hib contacts needing prophylaxis:** close, prolonged contact from 7 days before symptom onset until 48 hours after antibiotics — household contacts **only if the household contains a vulnerable contact**; childcare contacts with household-level contact who are themselves vulnerable; vulnerable contacts who shared a hospital room with the case; healthcare workers with unprotected close airway exposure and inadequate PPE.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vulnerable contact** = infant under 7 months (whatever the vaccination status) · immunocompromised or asplenic person of any age (whatever the vaccination status) · inadequately vaccinated child aged 7 months–2 years (childcare) or 7 months–5 years (household and hospital).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rifampicin, oral, daily for 4 days:** under 1 month 10 mg/kg; 1 month and over 20 mg/kg (max 600 mg).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pregnancy or rifampicin contraindicated: IM ceftriaxone daily for 2 days, 50 mg/kg (max 1 g).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Catch up Hib immunisation in any child who is behind.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **_Streptococcus pneumoniae_: no increased risk to contacts — no prophylaxis.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Rifampicin induces the metabolism of many drugs** — including the oral contraceptive pill (use alternative contraception), anticonvulsants, warfarin and chloramphenicol. **Do a drug interaction check.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use rifampicin with hepatic impairment.** It is preferred in infants, though ciprofloxacin is safe and effective.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Warn that rifampicin turns body fluids red** — urine, saliva, tears (can damage soft contact lenses), sweat.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23
